c53c3b080d69.title: RL learning framework for the guided exploration of crystalline materials.
c53c3b080d69.caption: a , Schematic of the latent diffusion framework with GRPO. The process shifts from standard likelihood-driven sampling (red path) to reward-guided exploration (green path), which enables the agent (denoising diffusion models) to navigate the latent space towards underexplored regions via flexible, multi-objective optimization. b , Continuous creativity reward matrix based on AMD, which is designed to penalize known or redundant structures while maximizing rewards for unique and new compounds. c , Stability reward mapping as a function of the predicted energy above the convex hull. The function guides the agent towards thermodynamically stable phases while penalizing unstable configurations. d , t -SNE projection of structural embeddings showing 1,000 reference (training) structures (grey density contours) and 500 generated structures coloured by the diversity reward. Here, Δ E F is the formation-energy difference; C 0 , C t and C T denote the initial, intermediate and terminal crystal states, respectively; q is the forward process; and p θ is the learned reverse process.

98f734cd6362.title: Example knowledge base entry and the JSON index summarizing method descriptions and file paths.
98f734cd6362.caption: Each KB entry is stored as a structured Markdown file containing the problem setup, issues addressed, core method, implementation code snippets, and critical hyperparameters. The JSON index holds a summary of all 70 entries (method name, brief description, and file path) and is used by the retriever agent to identify the most relevant KB entry for a given parent solution.

98f734cd6362.title: Multi-agent system performance improvements over single-agent baselines across six benchmark SciML problems.
98f734cd6362.caption: Each bar shows the improvement factor achieved by the multi-agent evolutionary framework over the single-agent root solution for one of the six benchmark problems: discontinuous function approximation (Func. Approx.), Poisson equation on an L-shaped domain (Poisson), Burgers equation using a physics-informed neural network (Burgers PINN), antiderivative operator learning (Antiderivative), multiple-input operator learning for a reaction-diffusion equation (Multi-input Op.), and 2D cylinder wake vorticity reconstruction (Cylinder Wake). The improvement factor is defined as the ratio of the root solution score to the champion solution score, where the score is a loss metric (lower is better); a higher improvement factor indicates a greater benefit from multi-agent collaboration, knowledge retrieval, and evolutionary search. The y-axis is displayed on a base-10 logarithmic scale. In all six experiments the multi-agent system achieves a lower score than the single-agent baseline, with improvement factors ranging from approximately 10 to over 11,000.

98f734cd6362.title: Agreement among selector agents for the top three nominations across all experiments.
98f734cd6362.caption: Each bar shows the fraction of experiments in which all three selector models—GPT-5 Mini, Grok-4 Fast, and Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash—cast identical votes for a given nomination rank. The x-axis shows the nomination rank (1st choice, 2nd choice, 3rd choice) and the y-axis shows the fraction of experiments (out of six total) in which the three selectors were unanimous. High agreement at the 1st-rank nomination reflects consistent identification of the best-performing candidate for exploitation. Lower agreement at the 3rd-rank nomination reflects healthy divergence in exploratory candidate selection, where selectors disagree on which lower-performing solution has the most potential for further improvement. The three bars correspond to the first, second, and third nomination ranks respectively.

98f734cd6362.title: Agent word-count contributions across all experiments.
98f734cd6362.caption: The stacked bar chart shows the total word count contributed by each planning agent type in each of the six experiments. The x-axis labels each experiment (Func. Approx., Poisson, Burgers PINN, Antiderivative, Multi-input Op., Cylinder Wake) and the y-axis shows total word count. Each colored stacked segment represents one agent type: Proposer, Critic, User, Retriever, and Result Analyst; the color assigned to each agent type is indicated in the figure legend. Engineering and selector agents are excluded. The Proposer agent contributes the largest share of words in all experiments, owing to its multi-round structured reasoning steps prior to and during proposal synthesis. The human user contributes less than 0.3% of the total generated text across all six experiments, demonstrating the high degree of autonomy of the multi-agent system.

98f734cd6362.title: Illustration of the ensemble-guided solution tree selection mechanism.
98f734cd6362.caption: The diagram shows a representative solution tree at one evolutionary iteration. Each node represents a candidate solution annotated with its score. The best-performing node currently on the tree (highlighted with a star) is always selected for mutation in the next iteration to ensure exploitation of the strongest known solution. One or more additional nodes are selected by majority vote among the selector ensemble (GPT-5 Mini, Grok-4 Fast, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash) to ensure exploration of alternative directions. Arrows connecting nodes indicate parent-child relationships produced by mutation. All selected parent nodes are mutated in parallel, each producing one child solution per iteration. Nodes that have reached the maximum number of children (10) are excluded from selection to prevent over-exploitation of a single branch.

8c775dd0753c.title: GFF-MAP workflow for GNN-based analysis of grain-level fatigue failure and micromechanical assessment of pores.
8c775dd0753c.caption: Schematic overview of the proposed framework in which graph neural network (GNN) models receive microstructural descriptors as input and are trained on crystal plasticity simulation data. Depending on the task, the GNNs are configured to perform either regression, predicting grain-level micromechanical fields, or classification, directly identifying fatigue critical pores. The network architecture and output layers are adapted according to the prediction objective.

8c775dd0753c.caption_zh: 图神经网络以微观结构描述符为输入，利用晶体塑性模拟数据训练；根据任务分别回归晶粒尺度的微观力学场，或分类识别影响疲劳的关键孔隙。网络结构与输出层随预测目标调整。

8c775dd0753c.title: Overview on the evolution in the performance of the GNN regression models for the prediction of grain-level σ Z Z , a v g , σ Z Z , m a x , w P , a v g , and w P , m a x , and potential strategies to identify critical pores.
8c775dd0753c.caption: The loss in performance going from grain-average to extreme values and from stress to fatigue damage indicator parameters is highlighted. The predicted w P , m a x was used to determine which pores are critical , then comparing these results against the predictions of the GNN model for the direct classification of the critical pores.

8c775dd0753c.title: Comparison of GNN predictions against crystal plasticity ground truth over the testing dataset for all four targeted micromechanical fields.
8c775dd0753c.caption: a , b report the results for σ Z Z , a v g ; c, d for σ Z Z , m a x ; e , f for w P , a v g ; and g , h for w P , m a x . The parity plots on the top row report data from all grains in the testing dataset, while the data in the bottom row is restricted only to the pore-adjacent grains. 8c775dd0753c.caption: a Crystal plasticity simulation, b GNN model predictions, and c Difference between the prediction and simulation. Three-dimensional views of the SEVM are presented in the top row, and two-dimensional slices of the mid-plane normal to the Z -direction, highlighting the region surrounding the pore, are shown in the bottom row.

8c775dd0753c.caption: a Crystal plasticity simulation, b GNN model predictions, c Difference between the prediction and simulation. 8c775dd0753c.caption: a Reports the predictions of the regression GNN-based approach, while b reports the predictions of the classification GNN-based approach.

8c775dd0753c.title: Relation between pore morphological properties (equivalent diameter and sphericity) and the fraction of the four SEVMs simulations for the same pore defect that are correctly predicted by the GNN-based surrogate models, for the 62 pores in the testing dataset.
8c775dd0753c.caption: a Reports the fraction of SEVMs where the fatigue hotspot predicted by crystal plasticity is located at the pore, as the ground-truth reference. b Reports the fraction of SEVMs correctly predicted by the regression-based approach, while c reports the same but for the predictions by the classification-based approach. The correctness of a prediction is evaluated independently on each SEVM, which is considered to be correctly predicted if the classification of the pore it contains as either critical or non-critical matches the results of crystal plasticity. The triangular markers refer to the pores that behave consistently across all four SEVMs, being either always critical or always non-critical .

8c775dd0753c.title: Relative importance of node and edge features for the regression GNN models.
8c775dd0753c.caption: Relative feature importance of a node features and b edge features. Histogram bars are colored based on the target micromechanical field ( σ Z Z , a v g , σ Z Z , m a x , w P , a v g , and w P , m a x ) they refer to. 8c775dd0753c.title: Relative importance of node and edge features for the classification GNN model.
8c775dd0753c.caption: Relative feature importance of a node features and b edge features. The features identified by * are applicable only to the grains neighboring the pore and refer to the change in that property due to pore insertion.

8c775dd0753c.title: Relationship between pore morphological properties (equivalent diameter and sphericity) and the fraction of the four SEVMs simulations for the same pore defect, where the fatigue hotspot, predicted by crystal plasticity, is located immediately adjacent to the pore.
8c775dd0753c.caption: Trends and correlations between pore geometry and the probability of being critical emerge, but it is evident that geometry alone is not sufficient to reliably predict whether a pore is prone to cause crack initiation, except in extreme cases.

fce3019b88c7.title: The AI-designed T-domain exhibits enhanced expression, solubility, and thermal stability compared to the wild-type domain.
fce3019b88c7.caption: a Expression levels of WT GxpS_T3 and AI-2 following induction in E. coli . b , Solubility analysis of WT GxpS_T3 and AI-2. Protein expression was induced with 0.05 mM IPTG, and cultures were incubated at 18 °C for 16 h. Soluble (S) and insoluble (I) fractions are shown. c Purification profiles of WT GxpS_T3 and AI-2. WT GxpS_T3 was purified under denaturing conditions due to insolubility, whereas AI-2 was recovered in soluble form. The experiments shown in a–c were performed in three independent biological replicates with similar results. d Thermal stability of WT GxpS_T3 and AI-2 was determined by thermal denaturation. The x-axis labels indicate the analyzed protein fractions: untreated AI-2, AI-2 purified under denaturing (urea) conditions, soluble AI-2 recovered after heat treatment (heat_sup), insoluble AI-2 recovered after heat treatment (heat_pellet), and WT GxpS_T3 purified under denaturing (urea) conditions. Bars represent mean values, and error bars indicate ± SD from three independent biological replicates, each representing the mean of three technical measurements. Source data are provided as a Source Data file.

fce3019b88c7.title: State-dependent interdomain interactions of WT GxpS_T3 and AI-2 T-domains across the NRPS catalytic cycle.
fce3019b88c7.caption: Structural representations and sequence alignments summarizing the distribution of persistent interdomain contacts identified from molecular dynamics simulations in the thiolation ( a ), condensation donor ( b ), and condensation acceptor ( c ) states. Structural views are shown below (WT GxpS_T3 left, AI-2 right), with corresponding sequence alignments displayed above. Interacting residues identified by molecular dynamics simulations are shown as sticks and highlighted in green (WT GxpS_T3) and cyan (AI-2), and are marked in the sequence alignment using the same color scheme. Only R residues were labeled in the structural representations. The T-domain is shown in orange, the adenylation (A) domain in blue, the condensation (C) domain in salmon, and the PPant arm in magenta. Major structural elements of the T-domain are labeled H1–H4. Interactions were defined as hydrogen bonds with ≥30% occupancy and/or distance-based contacts with ≥80% occupancy across simulation trajectories. Analyses are based on two independent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations per system and state ( n = 2). Complete hydrogen-bond and contact occupancy data are provided in Supplementary Data 1 .

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 1: Architectures of ANN models and their spiking counterparts. Schematic graph of standard neural architectures (MLP, PINN, and DeepONet) and their corresponding spiking implementations used in this work. The diagrams illustrate how conventional continuous activations are replaced by spiking neuron dynamics while preserving the overall network structure.

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 2: Parabola regression results. (a) Training loss history comparing the proposed QIF neuron model with direct spiking neural network training using LIF neurons. (b) Predicted solutions obtained from QIF and directly trained LIF networks compared with the ground truth parabola. (c) Predictions from QIF and ANN-to-SNN converted LIF networks. Zoomed regions highlight differences in approximation accuracy and smoothness.

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 8: Prediction errors for the (2 + 1)D Beltrami flow benchmark. QIF predictions produce smaller and more spatially localized errors, whereas LIF-based models exhibit larger and more diffuse error structures. Absolute error maps for velocity components at a representative time snapshot (t ≈0.692). (a) Errors for the u velocity component and (b) errors for the v velocity component. Results are shown for the proposed QIF model and ANN-to-SNN converted LIF networks with different simulation step sizes (32, 64 and 128), both without calibration (conv) and with calibration (cal).

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 3: Ricker wavelet regression results. QIF predictions remain smooth and closely match the ground truth, whereas LIF- based models exhibit structured error patterns. (a) Ground truth and predictions of u obtained using QIF neurons and directly trained LIF networks with different simulation step sizes. (b) Absolute error |u −ˆu| corresponding to (a). (c) Predictions for ANN-to-SNN converted LIF networks with 32 simulation steps. (d) Absolute error |v −ˆv| corresponding to (c).

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 4: DeepONet operator-learning results for the Poisson problem. (a) Training loss history comparing QIF neurons with directky trained LIF-based spiking networks using different simulation step sizes (32, 64, and 128 steps). (b) Example predicted solution curves for five test samples. Solid lines denote ground-truth solutions and dashed lines denote model predictions. (c) Distribution of per-sample root mean square error (RMSE) across the test set shown as a box-and-whisker plot.

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 5: PINN solution and derivative prediction for the 1D Poisson problem. Accurate computation of uxx is essential for enforcing the PDE residual in PINNs, and the figure highlights the degradation in derivative accuracy for LIF models compared with QIF training. (a) Predicted solution u(x) obtained using spiking neural networks trained with QIF neurons and ANN-to-SNN converted LIF models, shown both without calibration (conv) and with calibration (cali). For LIF conversion models, LIF-32, LIF-64 and LIF-128 correspond to simulations with 32, 64 and 128 time steps, respectively. (b) Predicted second derivative uxx(x) compared with the analytical ground truth.

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 6: PINN training with LIF neurons using surrogate gradient for the 1D Poisson problem. Although the boundary conditions are hard-coded, inaccuracies in the learned solution lead to large errors in the computed second derivative, which in turn produce significant residual violations across the domain. (a) Predicted solution u(x) obtained using direct PINN training with LIF neurons and surrogate gradients compared with the analytical ground truth. (b) Predicted second derivative uxx(x) computed from the learned solution. (c) Resulting PDE residual.

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 7: Burgers equation results for the (1+1)D problem. The QIF model accurately captures the solution profile and shock structure, while LIF-based models exhibit larger errors near the shock region. (a) Ground-truth solution and predictions produced by the QIF model and ANN-to-SNN converted LIF networks with different simulation step sizes (32, 64 and 128 steps), shown both without calibration (conv) and with calibration (cal). (b) Corresponding absolute error maps |u −ˆu|. (c) One-dimensional solution slices at two representative time instances (t = 0.45 and t = 0.75), comparing predicted solutions with the ground truth.

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 9: Spike generation dynamics of LIF and QIF neurons. Membrane potential evolution and spike generation for leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF, red) and quadratic integrate-and-fire (QIF, blue) neurons. LIF dynamics follow membrane integration up to a finite threshold and reset to rest voltage, whereas membrane potential of QIF neurons tend to infinity and reset to negative infinity.

6ca085b27ae8.title: 原文配图
6ca085b27ae8.caption: Figure 10: Phase evolution and spike generation in the phase representation. Phase ϕ(t) evolves linearly in time between incoming spikes and undergoes instantaneous upward jumps when input spikes arrive (orange segments). When the phase reaches the threshold ϕΘ, an output spike is emitted and the phase is reset to the starting point ϕreset = 0, corresponding to the beginning of a new cycle.

d10423960846.title: Data-driven framework.
d10423960846.caption: The proposed workflow integrates high-throughput micromagnetic simulations with forward and inverse machine learning to analyze the impact of nanostructure and phase properties on the coercivity of SmCo-1:7 permanent magnets. Note that the superscript `(P)' represents quantities of three different phases. E.g., \({M}_{{\rm{s}}}^{({\rm{P}})}\) represents \({M}_{{\rm{s}}}^{({\rm{M}})},\,{M}_{{\rm{s}}}^{({\rm{S}})}\) , and \({M}_{{\rm{s}}}^{({\rm{Z}})}\) , where superscripts `(M)', `(S)', and `(Z)' denote the cellular 2:17-phase (matrix), strip-shaped 1:5-phase, and platelet-shaped Z-phase, respectively.

d10423960846.title: Simulated hysteresis and forward neural networks.
d10423960846.caption: a Average half-cycle hysteresis and 95% confidence interval (CI 95% ) by micromagnetic simulation with ten reversal processes. b 1 - b 3 Transient domain structures with marked pinning sites at selected applied field strength. d10423960846.title: Inverse design of SmCo-1:7 nanostructures.
d10423960846.caption: a Schematic of the inverse design process. The inverse model ( i − NN) reads a set of queried values H c as input and Φ p and feeds back a set of nanostructural descriptors ( L , d , w S , and w Z ) as outputs, which are then fed into the forward model ( f − NN) for verification. Micromagnetic descriptors ( \(\alpha ,\,{M}_{{\rm{s}}}^{({\rm{P}})},\,{l}_{{\rm{dw}}{\prime} }^{({\rm{P}})}\) , and \({\sigma }_{{\rm{dw}}{\prime} }^{({\rm{P}})}\) , with `(P)' denoting quantities of three different phases), on the other hand, are prescribed during the training of the i − NN and inputs of the f − NN for verification. Parity plots of b H c and c Φ on inversely designed nanostructures vs. queried values. d 1 – d 3 Three inversely designed nanostructures based on queried H c and Φ p , respectively. The demagnetization curves from micromagnetic simulations used for validation are presented.

d10423960846.title: Angular dependence of the coercivity and inhomogeneity factor.
d10423960846.caption: Variation of coercivity H c with misorientation angle α for a different Cu contents in the 1:5-phase and b different Fe contents in the 2:17-phase. d10423960846.caption: Contour surface of H c and Φ p vs. characteristic distance ( L and d ) at various thickness of SmCo 5 and Sm 2 Co 1 7 phases: a w S = 3 nm, and b w S = 15 nm, with w Z = 2, 6, 10, respectively. Contour surfaces are also illustrated for various Cu/Fe contents: c Sm(Co 1− x Cu x ) 5 ( x Cu = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) and Sm 2 Co 1 7 phases, and d SmCo 5 and Sm 2 (Co 1− x Fe x ) 17 ( x Fe = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) phases, with fixed w S = 15 nm and w Z = 6 nm. Inset: Schematics of the nanoscopic phases and their corresponding nanostructural descriptors.

d10423960846.title: Phase fraction dependence of the coercivity and inhomogeneity factor.
d10423960846.caption: Contour surfaces of H c and Φ p vs. volume fractions φ S and φ Z of the corresponding phases with varying Cu/Fe contents: a H c and b Φ p with SmCo 5 and Sm 2 Co 1 7 phases, c H c and d Φ p with Sm(Co 0.7 Cu 0.3 ) 5 and Sm 2 Co 1 7 phases, and e H c and f Φ p with SmCo 5 and Sm 2 (Co 0.7 Fe 0.3 ) 17 phases.

d10423960846.title: Sensitivity analysis on nanostructural and micromagnetic descriptors.
d10423960846.caption: Barplots of relative feature importance of nanostructural and micromagnetic descriptors for H c and Φ p based on a Spearman correlation and b permutation test. c Hierarchical clustering of these quantities. Superscripts `(M)', `(S)', and `(Z)' denote the cellular 2:17-phase (matrix), strip-shaped 1:5-phase, and platelet-shaped Z-phase, respectively. For comparison, feature importance based on micromagnetic descriptor contrasts (red labels) and phase fraction (blue labels) is shown in d Spearman correlation and e permutation test, with the corresponding hierarchical clustering in f . Superscripts `(S-M)' and `(Z-M)' denote the contrasts between 1:5–2:17 and Z-2:17 phases, respectively. See definition in Eq. (6).

f55569d6c20b.title: Workflow of this study.
f55569d6c20b.caption: a Dataset establishment through LLM-powered literature mining and programmatic graph digitization. b Machine-learning-based framework integrating physics-guided descriptor engineering with a deep ensemble model for robust property prediction. c Discovery pipeline including high-throughput virtual screening to identify top candidates, followed by material synthesis and electrical characterization for experimental validation. The crystal-structure schematic in Fig. 1a was visualized using VESTA (Momma, K. & Izumi, F. VESTA 3 for three-dimensional visualization of crystal, volumetric and morphology data. J. Appl.
